rationale: The workflow is a multi-platform Docker delivery pipeline plus a Windows MSYS2 MSI build. I evaluated the applicable patterns against the repository files and workflow: P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is contraindicated because the matrix explicitly sets fail-fast: false, meaning every variant result is required; P-LIT-GHA-CACHE has no workflow-level dependency installation to cache (dependencies are encapsulated in the reusable docker-builder/docker-merge actions and MSYS2 scripts, and msys2/setup-msys2 already uses cache: false with update: true); no test step runs at the workflow level, so test prioritization/selection patterns do not apply; there is no schedule trigger, so schedule-suppression patterns do not apply; there is no Bazel build, so Bazel patterns do not apply; and a custom timeout would be speculative given only three successful runs with no per-job duration baseline and a risk of breaking valid slow Windows builds. No supported optimization fits while preserving the intended build and test coverage, so NO_CHANGE.
